newsitem.title: INDIA: At least 8 wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: At least 8 wounded in Kashmir grenade attack.

text.p: At least eight people were wounded on Wednesday when suspected separatist rebels hurled a grenade at a paramilitary post in a crowded marketplace in Kashmir, police said.
They said the grenade missed its target and exploded on the road in the busy Lal Chowk neighbourhood of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state. Most of the wounded were shoppers.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, police said.
Earlier, unidentified militants threw another grenade near the outskirts of Srinagar that did not explode and was later neutralised, police said.

More than a dozen rebel groups are waging a separatist revolt in Jammu and Kashmir, which is mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority state. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed since the rebellion broke out in 1990.
Eight people, six of them separatist guerrillas, have been killed in different gunbattles across the Kashmir Valley since Tuesday evening, a police spokesman said.
